chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Horace versus Fletcher as pianists
summary: Asked about Feather's claim that he was the more swinging Hines-style pianist, Horace says Fletcher played fast showpieces like Honeysuckle Rose while he preferred Sweet Lorraine-type tunes; he idolizes Fletcher's success.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Might be worth it. This -- again I'm using a Xerox copy, but I believe this is probably from Leonard Feather's Encyclopedia that I'm quoting now. This is concerning you. It says, "He" -- Horface -- "is acknowledged to have been a more swinging piano soloist in the Earl Hines manner than was Fletcher." You want to make any comment on that? That's putting you on the spot.

Fletcher was a great pianist, and he always liked more or less to play things that had a fast beat, just the opposite of what Ben Webster was like. And it showed off his execution, and, of course, when people came out to see Fletcher, naturally Henderson, in this way he could be flashy in playing the piano, like I know one of his feature numbers was Honeysuckle Rose, but at the tempo that he played it off, it showed him off well on the piano. And I just used to like things like "Sweet Lorraine," you know, where you --

Yeah, funky beats and (unintelligible) you could play in the right hand, if you wanna octaves, you know, (unintelligible). That was the difference. We had different styles, but it's just all in the matter of the way you thought, you know, and he thought his way, and I thought mine. A lot of things we thought alike, and -- but I idolize his way of thinking because he was successful. You don't fight find success; you just join it (unintelligible).
